title: I Am Absenting Myself from Myself
text:
I am absenting myself from myself.

Little by little, the ballast of dream gives way

to the double reality

that is my life in passage.

Another being inside my flesh

forges its flesh, its skin,

its tiny heart, my star!


I attend the silent splitting

with yearning astonishment, with the new

joy of seeing myself in other eyes of mine,

made from my eyes,

colored by my blood,

ah, by all that I am.


Day by day the heartbeat

is a blow that reminds me, urgent,

of courage I do not have,

of heroism I never dreamed.


And I fear for the one I am creating

in agreed mystery

inside my shoreless solitude,

near my heart, its star.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the pregnancy/self-division image and the child as star near the heart.

title: Growing in Densities, in Such a Way...
text:
Growing in densities, in such a way

that in a nearby century you will be solid.

Giant blue plinth with soft rose

wetting your skin in twilight.


All your malleable softness,

that now supports our bodies,

will set among its fragrant salts

and you will be whole, a polished track.


Who will go over your ground, then so tight

as now it is of oily liquid?

What creatures will you hear sliding,

drunk with you, through your infinity?


I sense you in the stone of yourself,

mineral your presence, which slowly,

fugitive, evaporates gently

its bodily thickness of seaweed and iodine.




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation preserves the Mar Menor imagined becoming mineral, solid, and still fragrant with salt.

title: This Sea Is a Clustered Sea...
text:
This sea is a clustered sea

in two arms of land, clamorous

with sirocco and southwest wind...; it is a thick

old wine of salts and iodine.


It is a sea for intact young people;

and it is a sea for beings who already know

what the sea carries in itself, from the land.

It is a sea without riders, it does not gallop.


And this smell of millennia smelled by

its shores of pines and palms

is of the sea upon the sea: it is already celestial

like the hands of lingering archangels.


Oh its light and its sound, its great clouds

that the east wind detaches from the skies

and overturns into the field, like rivers

returning from God, the bronze sea!




The Poems of Mar Menor, 1959
editorial_note: The translation keeps the Mar Menor as clustered bronze sea of salts, winds, and celestial shore-smell.

title: Gentlemen, I Know Well...
text:
Gentlemen, I know well

of poisons...



Gentlemen, I know well of the poisons

of literature:

the shameless and terrible tyranny

of an impure Beauty

that stains our lips with word,

our eyes with figure,

and the brain with dreams or sins,

in flagrant, diabolical imposture.

I desire it for no one, and no one

should ever desire it,

but blessed are those who submit

to its dark gaze.
editorial_note: The translation keeps Jodra's ironic warning against literature's poisonous beauty.

title: Proposal of the Fig
text:
I propose to you

the sweetness of the fig,

its rosy flesh,

folded and

moist

like a sea animal.


Enjoy the mystery of this fruit,

its mollusk texture,

its intimate

size.

Smooth,

its pulp

will press the desire

of your tongue.


I propose to you

the delights of the fig.

Bite its violated,

forsaken center,

taste again—stubborn—

its flesh

that

keeps honeys and deluges.


The delights and sweetness of the fig

—small and overflowing—

only this I

propose to you.

Let your deep mouth

linger

in the secret sweetness,

let it slowly assault

its unveiled flesh.


Let it bring to your palate

the memory

of primitive flavors.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the sensual fig invitation and its mollusk/sea-animal imagery.

editorial_note: This alternate-title variant preserves the embedded Fig Proposal heading and duplicate source body.

title: Tear Off the Gag!...
text:
Tear off the gag

and sing!


Spit out the poison

and live!


Put sadness

in the palm of your hand

and blow!


Bandage the wound

and fight!


Come on!


Now!
editorial_note: The translation keeps the imperative rhythm of survival and resistance.

title: Cynicism Has No Limits...
text:
Cynicism has no limits.

They imprison you, they beat you,

they isolate you in punishment dungeons

with rats, cockroaches

and other filth,

and on top of it they complain

because you scream.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the blunt indictment of carceral cruelty and official complaint.

title: Pantheons
text:
Pantheons for the living,

they call these

punishment cells,

but it will not be I

—I thought—

who transforms them

into "for the dead."

And if I am telling it,

it is because it was true.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the prison-cell pun and the survival proof in testimony.

title: Cell
text:
The air does not reach me.

Perhaps it is wandering lost

through those corridors

or is held incommunicado

in some cell,

punished

for wanting—like me—

to walk everywhere:

to go to the Soviet Union,

for example.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the personified air punished for wanting freedom of movement.
